title: Do Households React to Monetary Policy?
authors: You Li; Weiqiang Tan; Daifei Troy Yao; Jian Zhang
eligible_reason: Not a staggered binary DiD. Prosper loan listings (repeated cross-section of borrowers) around FOMC announcement dates: reghdfe rate_borrower post ffr_changeXpost (or ffr_surpriseXpost ffr_expectedXpost) $ctrl1 [$ctrl2], absorb(borrower_state policy_date prosper_rating [income_range employ_status occupation]), cluster borrower_state. post marks listings after an announcement and applies to all borrowers at each common policy date; the coefficient of interest is the continuous rate surprise x post (treatment intensity), with borrower controls in every column; RD-in-time variants restrict to |dday| <= window. Table 5 (Robinhood) regresses changes in holdings on continuous FFR surprises with firm controls. No units adopting a binary treatment at different dates.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe; 7-replication/Analysis.do (Tables 1-6, Figures 1-4), outputs in stata-output/. Data files analysis_p2p_main.dta and analysis_retail.dta are referenced but not included.
data_files_note: Readme: Prosper and Robinhood terms of use prohibit redistribution; Compustat/CRSP licensed. Package ships only code, logs, data dictionary and outputs.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). Continuous monetary-policy surprise x post at common FOMC dates; data not shipped.
